articles.title: Bellingham y la Bota que ni sabía que existía
articles.standfirst: El centrocampista inglés recibe dos meses después el premio que reconoce sus siete goles en el Mundial, donde terminó tercero en la tabla de goleadores
articles.summary: El centrocampista inglés recibe dos meses después el premio que reconoce sus siete goles en el Mundial, donde terminó tercero en la tabla de goleadores
articles.body: Jude Bellingham ya tiene en casa el recuerdo físico de su gran Mundial. La FIFA le ha entregado la Bota de Bronce, el premio que corresponde al tercer máximo goleador del torneo, después de que el centrocampista del Real Madrid terminara la competición con siete goles. Y su reacción al recibirla fue tan inesperada como sincera: no sabía ni que existía. “La Bota de Bronce del Mundial... No sabía ni que existía, pero gracias de todos modos”, escribió Bellingham junto a una imagen del trofeo en su aplicación JB5. El premio pone el broche individual a un Mundial en el que el madridista terminó codeándose con los grandes goleadores del campeonato. Kylian Mbappé acabó con 10 tantos, Lionel Messi con ocho y Bellingham con siete, empatado con Erling Haaland pero tercero en la clasificación por los criterios de desempate. Más allá de la medalla de bronce, los números explican la dimensión del torneo de Bellingham. Sus siete goles son la tercera mejor cifra de un inglés en la historia del Mundial, solo por detrás de Harry Kane (14) y Gary Lineker (10). Y hay otro dato todavía más significativo para el madridista: ningún centrocampista había marcado tantos goles en una misma edición de un Mundial. Bellingham además apareció cuando Inglaterra más lo necesitaba. Marcó dos goles contra México en octavos y otros dos ante Noruega en cuartos, convirtiéndose en uno de los pocos ingleses capaces de firmar dobletes en dos eliminatorias consecutivas. Solo Pelé había conseguido hacerlo siendo más joven.

images.caption: Jude Bellingham celebra su tanto frente a Panamá.

articles.title: Forlán debuta en Uruguay sin Valverde y con una cruel derrota ante Japón... en el centenario de Giménez
articles.standfirst: Los goles de Shiogai y Ueda, ya en el añadido, provocan la derrota de 'La Celeste'
articles.summary: Los goles de Shiogai y Ueda, ya en el añadido, provocan la derrota de 'La Celeste'
articles.body: Había expectación, mucha, por asistir al debut de Diego Forlán con Uruguay. El ex de Atlético y Villarreal, que ejercerá de seleccionador interino -dirigirá también a la sub 20- hasta marzo, no pudo estrenarse con victoria: sufrió una cruel derrota, en el tiempo de descuento, ante Japón (3-1). Sin Fede Valverde, lesionado, introdujo dos variantes importantes respecto al último partido de Marcelo Bielsa, que acabó con derrota ante España (0-1). Cambió el esquema -dibujó un 1-4-4-2 en detrimento del 1-4-1-4-1- e introdujo seis cambios en un once del que se 'cayeron' Muslera, Varela, Cáceres, Ugarte, Cannobio y el ya citado Valverde. 'El Cacha' alineó de inicio a Mele en portería; Nández, Ronald Araujo, Mathías Olivera y Sanabria en defensa; Brian Rodríguez, Torreira, Bentancur y Maxi Araujo en el medio; y formó arriba con Fede Viñas y Darwin Núñez. Golpeó primero Japón, en el 11'. Keito Nakamura cambió de banda y Kuryu Matsuki hizo el resto. Recibió pegado a banda, tiró la diagonal hacia el medio y sorprendió a Mele con un zurdazo ajustado al palo desde la frontal. Empató Uruguay en el 42', al borde del descanso por medio de Maxi Araujo. Robó altó 'La Celeste' y Hayakawa logró salvar el mano a mano con Viñas. Sin embargo, el carrilero/extremo de Sporting CP logró rehacerse para recoger el rechace y marcar sin demasiado ángulo. Le sentaron mejor los cambios a Japón -dio entrada a Kamada, Ueda, Kubo, Junnosuke Suzuki, Junya Ito, Ao Tanaka, Soma y Shiogai- que a Uruguay, que metió a Zalazar, De Arrascaeta, Giménez, Juan Rodríguez, Aguirre, Bernal, Piquerez y Pellistri. Fue, sin duda, un encuentro especial para Jose María Giménez. El central del Deportivo -cedido por el Atlético- alcanzó las 100 internacionalidades -suma ocho goles- con Uruguay. Mucho ha llovido ya desde que Óscar Washington Tabárez le diera la alternativa el 11 de septiembre de 2013, con 18 años, siete meses y 22 días, en la victoria sobre Colombia (2-0) en las Eliminatorias Sudamericanas. El partido parecía destinado a acabar en empate hasta que apareció Kento Shiogai en el 92'. Ito rompió la defensa con un pase al 'lado débil' y el atacante del Wolfsburgo marcó -al límite del fuera de juego- tras una rápida pared con Ayase Ueda. Hubo tiempo, aún, para que Ueda anotase el definitivo 3-1 en el 97'. Recibió un pase al hueco de Ito y marcó a puerta vacía tras eludir la salida del meta Mele. Un final 'cruel', pero la Uruguay de Forlán aún tiene margen de mejora.

images.caption: Diego Forlán, en el banquillo de Uruguay. INSTAGRAM

articles.title: Ancelotti se moja con Vinicius y Raphinha: "Están en momentos diferentes"
articles.standfirst: El seleccionador de Brasil confirma que el azulgrana está haciendo algo espectacular mientras que el madridista reconoce que puede que no esté en su mejor momento
articles.summary: El seleccionador de Brasil confirma que el azulgrana está haciendo algo espectacular mientras que el madridista reconoce que puede que no esté en su mejor momento
articles.body: Carlo Ancelotti compareció este jueves en rueda de prensa en Townsville, a las puertas del primer amistoso de la nueva era post-Mundial de Brasil ante Australia. El italiano, que adelantó el 11 inicial de su selección, no tuvo inconveniente a la hora de hablar de dos las estrellas de su equipo y de la LaLiga: Vinicius y Raphinha. Carletto valoró muy positivamente el arranque de temporada del atacante del Barça, que está firmando números de otro planeta como falso 9: 14 goles y tres asistencias en solo ocho partidos. "Raphinha está haciendo algo espectacular en una posición que no era la suya, aunque ahora parece que también lo es", sentenció Ancelotti, dejando claro que el brasileño se ha adueñado de una demarcación que ni siquiera es la suya de origen. Dejando claro previamente que el azulgrana y Vinicius pasan por momentos distintos, el italiano dejó claro que, aunque el madridista "puede que no atraviese por su mejor momento, confiamos en que ambos serán jugadores clave para el futuro", zanjó el italiano. El propio Ancelotti confirmó que Vini y Raphinha no solo serán titulares el viernes, sino que compartirán delantera con Endrick y Estevao, formando un cuarteto ofensivo de máxima intensidad para medirse a los locales en el Queensland Country Bank Stadium. El 11 de Brasil lo compondrán: "Hugo Souza; Matheuzinho, Marquinhos, Vitor Reis, Douglas Santos; Danilo, Bruno Guimarães; Estêvão, Raphinha, Endrick, Vinícius Júnior".

articles.title: Konaté, bajo vigilancia: una rodilla con más de 100 días de baja que "hay que gestionar"
articles.standfirst: El jugador ya sufrió con el Liverpool dos lesiones en la articulación que ha provocado que tenga que abandonar la selección
articles.summary: El jugador ya sufrió con el Liverpool dos lesiones en la articulación que ha provocado que tenga que abandonar la selección
articles.body: Konaté se ha vuelto de la selección lesionado, pero con un parte médico que no resulta especialmente alarmante: un leve esguince en la rodilla derecha. El informe, que el Madrid deberá confirmar, y lo extenso del parón de selecciones, amortiguan el golpe que supone la baja del central. Pero hay un problema 'oculto' que los servicios médicos del Madrid deberán comprobar y que puede estar detrás del motivo de que al jugador se le haya liberado de la selección "por precaución" para no correr riesgos. Konaté ya sufrió dos lesiones importantes en la rodilla derecha dañada ahora. Estando en el Liverpool, el defensa estuvo 110 días de baja por problemas en dicha articulación. Ambos hace tiempo, pero lo suficientemente importantes como para tenerlos en cuenta. El primer episodio, y el más grave, lo sufrió el 31 de julio de 2022, en un amistoso contra el Estrasburgo. En el choque con un rival, la rodilla derecha sufrió una hiperextensión que le obligó a estar más de dos meses de baja, 70 días concretamente. Una lesión que en aquella temporada vino acompañada de dos lesiones musculares más que le arruinaron el año. Dos años más tarde, sufriría el segundo daño en la rodilla derecha. Prácticamente en la última jugada del partido de Champions ante el Real Madrid, el 27 de noviembre de 2024, Konaté se lesionó en una acción con Endrick. El central acabó el partido cojeando y finalmente se confirmó la lesión, que le dejó mes y medio sin jugar (40 días). En el comienzo de la pasada temporada, en la recta final de un partido ante el Arsenal, fue sustituido por precaución por molestias en la rodilla derecha, pero finalmente todo quedó en un susto. "Los servicios médicos de la selección francesa han actuado de acuerdo a unos criterios médicos absolutamente correctos, al preservar al futbolista de un empeoramiento en la lesión. Son ahora los médicos del Madrid los que tendrán que valorar el tratamiento", afirma el reconocido traumatólogo Pedro Luis Ripoll. El doctor reconoce que este tipo de lesiones, como las sufridas por Konaté, pueden dejar 'huellas' y hay que tenerlas siempre presentes: "Se puede tratar de una inestabilidad funcional, algún tipo de inflamación articular producto de una inestabilidad funcional-transitoria, que podría tener su origen en las lesiones que sufrió con anterioridad y que ocasionaron tantos días de baja. Es una situación que hay que gestionar". El doctor Ripoll también lanza una advertencia en este tipo de lesiones por la pérdida propiocepción. "Es cuando se produce una interrupción en el control automático que el cerebro ejerce sobre la articulación. El jugador puede estar físicamente recuperado, pero si no recupera la propiocepción, su articulación no responderá de forma refleja ante un mal apoyo. Hay que 'reconectar' para que se contraigan todo los músculos que hacen que la rodilla no sufra un episodio de inestabilidad que conllevaría una posible lesión. Es la parte más importante de la readaptación. La posibilidad de lesiones musculares también están vinculadas a la propiocepción", explica Ripoll.

images.caption: A la izquierda, imagen de la lesión de 2022, y a la derecha, la de 2024.

articles.title: Week 4 college football viewer's guide: Loaded Saturday slate features 6 games between ranked teams, including Texas at Tennessee
articles.summary: Four of those games are in the SEC and the other two are in the Big Ten.
articles.body:
Week 4 is the biggest weekend of the 2026 college football season.

Saturday features six matchups between teams ranked in the AP Top 25. Four of those come in the SEC and the other two are in the Big Ten. We won't filibuster any longer. Here are the games to watch this weekend.

The winner gets to be called UT for the rest of the year. The loser has to find another acronym.

It's the biggest game of young Tennessee QB Faizon Brandon's career and he's shown why he won the starting QB job as a true freshman through the first three games. Brandon has yet to throw an interception and has nine total touchdowns; he's thrown for six and rushed for three.

Two of those games have come against Furman and Kennesaw State , so it's hard to judge just how good the Volunteers offense actually is this season. But it's a promising sign that Tennessee has been able to dominate its opponents on the ground no matter who it has played. In a 45-24 win over Georgia Tech , the Vols rushed 45 times for 299 yards.

That takes pressure off Brandon; he was 10-of-21 passing for 148 yards and two scores against the Yellow Jackets. Is that run game sustainable against the Longhorns? Teams are averaging just 3.4 yards a carry against Texas this season and Ohio State had 94 yards on 31 carries.

Auburn transfer Cam Coleman hasn't caught more than four passes in a game so far the season for Texas, but he's scored twice against both Texas State and UTSA. Arch Manning is averaging under seven yards an attempt through the first three games of the season and Tennessee's opponents have thrown for just 453 yards all season.

The Rebels' status as an underdog isn't a sign of disrespect to a top-five team. Rather, it's more about how good Florida has looked through the first three weeks of Jon Sumrall's tenure.

The Gators were the clear better team in their win over Auburn as Jadan Baugh has established himself as one of the best running backs in the country. Baugh has 458 yards and eight touchdowns already this season and is averaging 8.5 yards every time he carries the ball. Teams haven't been afraid to run the ball against Ole Miss so far this season, either. Charlotte's 33 attempts are the fewest of any Ole Miss opponent and LSU rushed for 172 yards and two scores in the Rebels' 32-24 win in Week 3.

It's also a potential letdown spot for Ole Miss. The game against LSU was such a focal point since the schedule was released that it's only natural to think the Rebels won't be as up for this game. Will that be rooted in any basis in reality? We'll know on Saturday.

We may also need to wait until Saturday to know about Ole Miss RB Kewan Lacy 's status. He re-injured his surgically repaired left shoulder in the win over LSU and missed the end of the game. JT Lindsey was effective in Lacy's absence, but Ole Miss is a much better football team with its star on the field. Having Lacy out there and effective helps Trinidad Chambliss share the playmaking burden.

This game has all the potential in the world to satiate your desires for old-school football. The over/under of 38.5 is the lowest of any game offered at BetMGM in Week 4.

No one is giving up fewer points per game than Iowa through three weeks. The Hawkeyes have shut out Northern Illinois and Northern Iowa — at least Michigan doesn't have "north" in its name — and allowed 13 points to Iowa State in Week 2. Those three teams have put up just 177 yards per game.

Hank Brown has taken over as Iowa's starting quarterback after a competition with Jeremy Hecklinski that went all the way to Week 1. The former Auburn QB is 45-of-62 passing for 473 yards and three touchdowns. Those are explosive numbers compared to the passing offense that Iowa has had in recent seasons.

The biggest question may actually come at running back, where both Kamari Moulton and L.J. Phillips missed the Week 3 win. Moulton and Phillips are the Hawkeyes' top running backs. Iowa didn't need them against its FCS foe, but will need at least one available on Saturday.

Michigan's offense finally broke free in the second half of a 52-17 win over UTEP in Week 3. After scoring 30 points over the first two weeks of the season, the Wolverines nearly matched that number with four touchdowns in the third quarter alone.

Will that game be a turning point for an offense that had looked stuck for the better part of 10 quarters? There are few questions about the Michigan defense. The ceiling for the Wolverines will be entirely determined by just how good the offense can be.

Some of the luster disappeared from this game as both teams lost in Week 3. Texas A&M's home loss to Kentucky was entirely unexpected. And it wasn't a fluke, either. The Wildcats bossed the Aggies .

Texas A&M lost receiver Terry Bussey for the season with a right leg injury on the opening kickoff. That puts more pressure on Mario Craver and Isaiah Horton to be the primary playmakers for an Aggies passing game that looks to need a robust support system around quarterback Marcel Reed . Craver and Horton have combined to catch 31 of the 62 completions Reed has thrown this season and all but one of his touchdown passes.

Reed emerged as Texas A&M's quarterback in this game two seasons ago as he came off the bench to rush for three scores in a 38-23 win. This season, he's completing less than 60% of his passes.

Sam Leavitt is still looking for his first great game as LSU's starting quarterback. Leavitt has thrown at least one interception in each of the Tigers' first three games and has five interceptions to just three touchdown passes. He's supplemented that total with six rushing touchdowns, but Leavitt needs to be a better passer for the Tigers' playoff hopes to become reality.

And the playoff is going to be a central theme of this game. The loser will drop to 2-2 and likely have no path to the postseason with another loss.

This is another game with some serious playoff implications, especially for an Oregon team that already has a loss thanks to that Week 2 defeat at Oklahoma State.

Even if it'd be a victory over a .500 Oregon team, a win would be a defining one for this Big Ten version of USC. The Trojans haven't threatened to be in the top tier of the conference since making the move from the Pac-12. Yes, there was a home win over Michigan in 2025, but that Wolverines team finished with five losses.

As always, there are still questions about the USC defense. The Trojans shut out Fresno State in a dominant Week 1 performance. But they've otherwise allowed 26 points in each of the other three games and 75 points combined over the past two weeks. The 35 points Rutgers scored in Week 3 was just seven fewer than the Scarlet Knights ' combined total over the first two weeks of the season.

If Oregon's offense has the same tells that it allegedly did against Oklahoma State, former TCU coach Gary Patterson's unit can tee off. But if the Portland State game was some much-needed corrective action, the Ducks could easily be the third straight team to drop 30 or more against the Trojans. If that happens and USC still wins, QB Jayden Maiava is going to get a lot of Heisman love. Through four games, Maiava is completing 76% of his passes for 1,173 yards and 12 TDs to just one interception.

Clemson (1-) at Cal (10:30 p.m. ET Friday, ESPN): We've got some serious ACC-after-dark potential with this one. Cal CB Kingston Lopa added a fifth interception against Wagner in Week 3 and will be licking his chops at the prospect of facing freshman Tait Reynolds in his first road start. Reynolds was much better after Clemson's win over North Carolina resumed following a lengthy weather delay.

Oklahoma at No. 2 Georgia (-14) (3:30 p.m. ET, ESPN): The Sooners are big underdogs as their offense has struggled so far this season. Tackle Michael Fasusi is unlikely to play along with star defensive lineman David Stone . That could be a recipe for disaster against a Georgia team that has dominated everyone it has played so far this season. Will Gunner Stockton 's run of throwing more touchdowns than incompletions this season continue?

Boise State (-7) at Western Michigan (3:30 p.m. ET, ESPN2): The midday slate is absolutely loaded this week. The College Football Playoff committee is going to pay close attention to this matchup of Broncos if Boise State and Western Michigan end up as two of the top non-power conference contenders in November. A home upset will go a long way to validating WMU's Week 1 loss — or "loss" if you prefer — to Michigan.

No. 15 Utah (-8) at Iowa State (3:30 p.m. ET, Fox): Given the roster overhaul that went on at Iowa State this offseason, oddsmakers are giving the Cyclones some credit. Opposing offenses are averaging just 226 yards per game against Iowa State this season. Utah is averaging more than that per game on the ground alone.

No. 19 Missouri at No. 24 Mississippi State (-6) (7:45 p.m. ET, SEC Network): Putting this game outside the top five shows just how loaded this weekend is. Mississippi State QB Kamario Taylor 's star turn will only get brighter with a big game against Mizzou and a win will be further evidence that this hot September isn't going to be a mirage for the Bulldogs. Last year, MSU started 4-0 before losing seven of their final eight regular-season games.

articles.title: Lola Gallardo se une a OnlyFans
articles.standfirst: La jugadora del Atlético de Madrid acercará su vida dentro y fuera del campo a los aficionados
articles.summary: La jugadora del Atlético de Madrid acercará su vida dentro y fuera del campo a los aficionados
articles.body: la capitana y guardameta del Atlético de Madrid, Lola Gallardo, ha anunciado este jueves su 'fichaje' por OnlyFans para ofrecer a los aficionados una visión exclusiva de su vida tanto dentro como fuera del campo. La internacional española ha construido una carrera distinguida al más alto nivel del fútbol, siendo campeona de Europa con el OL Lyonnes en 2020 y formando parte de la selección española en los Mundiales de 2025 y 2019, así como en las Eurocopas de 2013, 2017 y 2022. Además, ganó el Trofeo Zamora en 2024. A través de su plataforma OnlyFans, Lola acercará a los aficionados a la realidad de la vida como futbolista profesional, ofreciendo una mirada exclusiva y entre bastidores a su temporada y al camino hacia sus objetivos. Los aficionados verán las realidades de los entrenamientos, la preparación para los días de partido y todos los momentos cuando Lola está fuera del terreno de juego. También compartirá un lado más personal de su vida más allá del campo mientras se prepara para dar la bienvenida a su primer hijo con su esposa, Cristina Vicente. Los aficionados podrán conocer sus pasiones por la cocina, el pádel, la moda y viajar por el mundo con su familia. "El fútbol femenino está ganando popularidad enormemente y es un momento increíblemente emocionante para formar parte del fútbol. Aún queda mucho por hacer para acercar a los aficionados a las jugadoras y a las historias que hay detrás del deporte. Por eso estoy muy ilusionada de unirme a OnlyFans. Mi plataforma ofrece otro espacio donde los seguidores pueden seguir mi recorrido a lo largo de la temporada, conocerme fuera del campo y conectar con el mundo más amplio del fútbol femenino. Ofreceré una visión de mi vida como jugadora, con la vista puesta en la Champions League 2027/28 y celebrando a la comunidad que rodea el fútbol", aseguró la protagonista al anunciar el acuerdo con la plataforma. Lola Gallardo se une así a un grupo de atletas de clase mundial que ya están en OnlyFans como las boxeadoras Shannon Courtenay y Shauna Browne, la tenista Chloe Paquet y la luchadora de MMA Shauna Bannon.

articles.title: La sub 18 remonta en su estreno suizo
articles.standfirst: España se sobrepone al gol inicial de Costa de Marfil y firma tres puntos en el debut de la UEFA Friendship Cup, primer ensayo serio de cara al Mundial sub-17 de Catar
articles.summary: España se sobrepone al gol inicial de Costa de Marfil y firma tres puntos en el debut de la UEFA Friendship Cup, primer ensayo serio de cara al Mundial sub-17 de Catar
articles.body: Tres puntos y una lección de carácter. La selección española sub-18 se estrenó con victoria en la UEFA Friendship Cup pese a empezar por detrás en el marcador, en un debut ante Costa de Marfil que exigió paciencia y remontada a partes iguales. El torneo, que hasta el 3 de octubre reúne en Nyon a ocho de las mejores selecciones de la categoría del mundo, llega además en un momento clave: es uno de los grandes ensayos de esta generación antes del Mundial sub-17 que se disputa en Catar del 19 de noviembre al 13 de diciembre, la gran cita del curso para la base española. La hornada que dirige David Cubillo, la de los nacidos en 2009, afronta el reto de conquistar el único Mundial que le falta a la RFEF en sus vitrinas. Cada partido en Suiza es, por tanto, algo más que una amistad. Es un examen con vistas a Catar. Y el primero se saldó con nota, aunque obligara a sufrir. El rival, un combinado marfileño de despliegue físico notable, forzó a España a un ejercicio de insistencia. El conjunto español asumió el mando desde el pitido inicial, monopolizó la posesión y buscó grietas en una defensa africana replegada y correosa. Curro Navarro avisó primero y Jorge Domínguez rozó el gol de cabeza tras un córner, pero el muro marfileño aguantó y, sobre todo, golpeó cuando menos se esperaba. En la única ocasión que Costa de Marfil inquietó de verdad antes del descanso, la aprovechó. Alex N'dre rompió por velocidad y su pase de la muerte lo transformó Diarrassouba a placer. Un tiro, un gol, y España al vestuario con el marcador en contra y la sensación de pagar cara su falta de puntería. La reanudación trajo a una selección lanzada. Miguel Romero pudo igualar en una doble ocasión que salvó el meta Keita, y entre medias Darlington respondió a la única contra marfileña para mantener con vida a los suyos. La igualada, merecida, llegó en el 65. Owen Emeka se echó el equipo a la espalda por la derecha, su centro encontró a Yeremaiah Ramos en el área y el delantero no perdonó. Con el partido enderezado, España fue a por más. Encadenó posesiones, secó los contragolpes que tanto habían dolido y encerró al rival en su campo. El premio definitivo lo puso Roberto Tomás con un pase filtrado que Eloi Gómez resolvió con un disparo raso, ajustado y ganador. De ir a remolque a llevarse los tres puntos con autoridad. El estreno deja buenas sensaciones y una prueba mayúscula a la vista: el domingo 27, a las 18:00, aguarda Brasil en el Centre sportif de Colovray. Medirse a la pentacampeona del mundo dirá mucho del techo de esta selección, que cerrará la primera fase del torneo el miércoles 30 ante Canadá.

images.caption: Selección española sub-18 en la UEFA Friendship Cup 2026. RFEF

articles.title: El resurgir de Yáñez: una joya en el 'equipo' de Nico Paz, admirador de CR7 y rumbo a la leyenda en la Youth
articles.standfirst: El extremo del Castilla firma dos semanas gloriosas que lo catapultan otra vez tras un periodo 'extraño'
articles.summary: El extremo del Castilla firma dos semanas gloriosas que lo catapultan otra vez tras un periodo 'extraño'
articles.body: "Lo de Yáñez no se entiende", apuntaban semanas atrás en Valdebebas tras una de las suplencias del jugador con el Castilla. Un escaso protagonismo que venía siendo habitual desde el final de la temporada pasada. Justo tras coronarse campeón de la Youth League. Suplente en los dos últimos partidos del filial con la promoción de ascenso en juego y ocho minutos jugados en la eliminatoria para subir ante el Sabadell. Sólo su participación en el Bernabéu a las órdenes de Arbeloa ante el Oviedo (la segunda tras el Elche, donde firmó una asistencia) y la conquista del Europeo sub 19 con España, aliviaron un final de campaña agridulce. A la vuelta, ningún protagonismo con Mou en pretemporada y dos suplencias en los primeros cuatro partidos de Liga del Castilla. Un periodo 'extraño' con el que Yáñez ha acabado de un plumazo tras firmar dos semanas gloriosas: el 8 de septiembre hizo un doblete en la Youth para dar el triunfo al Madrid ante el Inter, el 19 marcó en la Copa Intercontinental y fue una pesadilla para el Wanderers, provocando la expulsión que allanó el camino al título, y ayer marcó un golazo con el Castilla tras una asociación mágica con Thiago Pitarch. Tres fogonazos consecutivos que lo catapultan nuevamente en su condición de una de las grandes joyas de La Fábrica. Y todo ello en una temporada en la que va camino de convertirse en leyenda de la Youth League como jugador con más partidos en la historia de la competición. En su cuarta temporada en la 'Champions juvenil', el extremo ha disputado ya 24 partidos y está a sólo cuatro del récord: los 28 de Pedro Álvaro (Benfica). Antes de su corto 'apagón', Yáñez estuvo muy de moda en Valdebebas. El extremo, representado por DC Global, la misma agencia de Nico Paz, vivió su 'boom' en la temporada 24-25, cuando siendo juvenil de segundo año debutó con Raúl en el Castilla y con Ancelotti en el Real Madrid. Su día de gloria con el primer equipo fue el 7 de diciembre de 2024, contra el Girona, con el 42 a la espalda y dejando una gran frase: "Cuando nací ya era del Real Madrid". Ancelotti le hizo debutar, pero su gran valedor fue Arbeloa, con el que protagonizó un increíble viaje por La Fábrica hasta el primer equipo. Yáñez fue titular en el primer once oficial del técnico al frente del Infantil A en 2019 y juntos alcanzaron la cima del Real Madrid. "Me puedo morir tranquilo después de una noche como esta", confesó Arbeloa tras hacer jugar a Yáñez en el Bernabéu ante el Elche siendo técnico del primer equipo. La salida de Arbeloa del Castilla, primero, y del primer equipo, después, fueron especialmente dolorosa para el jugador. Yáñez ruge otra vez con fuerza tras superar un pequeño bache. Y no es la primera vez que lo hace. Momentos malos siempre hay, pero el extremo tiene la fórmula para superarlos: CR7. Yáñez vivió un día especialmente amargo en el comienzo de la temporada 24-25 fallando dos penaltis en un mismo partido. Fue en la tercera jornada de Liga con el Juvenil A. El meta del Móstoles, Mario, fue una pesadilla para el extremo, que no se lo podía creer cuando le detuvo el segundo lanzamiento. El equipo de Arbeloa acabó goleando en ese partido tras un nuevo recital de fútbol del que fue gran protagonista Yáñez, pero al 7 blanco nada ni nadie le podía quitar el disgusto tras su doble fallo desde los once metros. La amargura del canterano tuvo su extensión en las redes sociales. "Estás hecho para continuar", rezaba una frase acompañada de una imagen de Cristiano Ronaldo cabizbajo y sentado sobre el césped. Un mensaje motivador para dar carpetazo al asunto y mirar hacia adelante. Como ha hecho en esta última ocasión.

articles.title: Manchester United put its iconic Old Trafford pitch up for sale, fans can now buy a piece for $165
articles.summary: Get a piece of Manchester United's iconic Old Trafford pitch! Limited keepsakes available for fans after the pitch renovation. Buy now for $165.
articles.body: Manchester United have found a rather unusual way to let supporters take a piece of Old Trafford home with them. After the stadium's famous playing surface was stripped back and rebuilt this summer, sections of the old turf were preserved rather than discarded, and they have now been turned into a limited keepsake for supporters willing to pay £125 ($165).Fans can now own a literal piece of Old TraffordManchester United supporters can now buy preserved pieces of the club's famous pitch, with the turf placed inside glass cubes and sold exclusively through the United Store for £125 ($165).The idea gives fans the chance to own a physical fragment of a stadium that has hosted some of the most significant moments in the club's history, rather than simply buying another piece of Manchester United merchandise. The preserved sections come from the playing surface that was removed during a major redevelopment project earlier this year.Old Trafford has been Manchester United's home for generations and witnessed the club's most successful period under Sir Alex Ferguson, when United won 13 Premier League titles, two Champions League trophies and numerous FA Cups.The same pitch also saw some of the club's more painful afternoons, including the 5-0 defeat to bitter rivals Liverpool and a 6-1 loss to Tottenham.More recently, the surface was involved in another memorable setback when United surrendered a 2-0 lead against Brighton in the Carabao Cup before losing 3-2. That defeat marked the first time in 42 years that Manchester United had lost a home match after leading at half-time.Now, supporters can own a small piece of the ground on which all of those moments unfolded.The pitch was stripped back to its foundations for the first time in 14 yearsThe turf being sold was preserved after Old Trafford underwent its most extensive pitch work in more than a decade.According to Manchester United's official club media, the entire pitch was dug up and stripped back to its foundation in June, marking the first time that the surface had undergone that process in 14 years.The project was completed by award-winning groundsperson Tony Sinclair and his team of experts, with the work designed to allow the playing surface to be regrown with two specific priorities in mind: improving player welfare and improving water drainage.Rather than simply throwing away sections of the old surface once the excavation was complete, the club carefully preserved parts of it and placed them inside glass cubes.Those cubes are now being sold exclusively through the United Store, turning material removed during a routine but significant stadium project into a collector's item for Manchester United supporters.For £125 ($165), fans therefore get more than a conventional souvenir, with the club offering them an actual piece of the Old Trafford playing surface that witnessed decades of victories, defeats and defining moments.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Álex Corredera: "Vamos a demostrar en el derbi que vamos muy en serio"
articles.standfirst: El centrocampista catalán vivirá su primer duelo asturiano con la camiseta del Sporting
articles.summary: El centrocampista catalán vivirá su primer duelo asturiano con la camiseta del Sporting
articles.body: Las primeras veces no se olvidan. Tiene toda la pinta de no hacerlo Alexandre Corredera. El centrocampista del Sporting de Gijón se estrenará en un derbi asturiano este domingo en el Carlos Tartiere. Ajeno a la presión, el '14' rojiblanco se toma el partido con la responsabilidad de brindar una alegría a la afición gijonesa tras 25 años sin ganar al Real Oviedo en su estadio. "Es una oportunidad enorme de dar un paso muy grande, de demostrar que vamos muy en serio. Estamos para intentar hacer algo histórico este año y empieza el domingo", contó en una entrevista concedida a Radio MARCA Asturias. Corredera apunta al once titular del Sporting al igual que ya lo ha hecho en las seis jornadas previas. El catalán tiene fijado, al igual que todo el vestuario, el partido ante el Oviedo en su calendario. "Soy un afortunado de poder jugar este tipo de partidos. Con las ganas y la ilusión por bandera, hay que ir por todo", dijo un Corredera que ya ha jugado el derbi canario con el Tenerife. "No es comparable a otro derbi. Lo que voy a vivir este domingo es mucho más fuerte y especial", aseguró. También trasladó el mediocentro un mensaje ambicioso de cara a lo que ocurrirá este domingo en el Carlos Tartiere. Un discurso que se mantiene en el vestuario del Sporting desde el inicio de la semana. "Vamos a meter alma y corazón para que la gente se sienta orgullosa. Seguro que a las 11 de la noche estaremos celebrando", vaticinó Corredera. Un futbolista que también reconoció en la entrevista haber visualizado muchos partidos del Oviedo esta temporada. A modo de análisis, sobre el rival reconocía Corredera que "va a ir creciendo durante las semanas". De todos modos, el centrocampista puso el foco en su Sporting. "Si estamos a buen nivel con y sin balón, le debemos hacer daño. Va a ser un partido con matices, muy difícil. Ellos vienen de una derrota y cambiarán cosas. Nosotros hemos trabajado mucho pensando en nosotros", verbalizó el catalán. Otro protagonista especial este domingo por la noche en tierras ovetenses será Guille Rosas. El lateral, formado en la cantera de Mareo, afrontará el derbi con una motivación especial: alcanzará en el Carlos Tartiere los 200 partidos con la camiseta del Sporting. En la previa del derbi asturiano, Guille Rosas habló sobre el cambio de discurso entre los dos equipos con un mensaje más ambicioso desde Gijón. "Puede ser que haya cambiado. Con los primeros derbis que jugué, ellos venían del fútbol no profesional y teníamos el sentimiento de superioridad. Eso ha dado la vuelta. Somos un equipo humilde, que sabemos lo que representamos. No somos crecidos ni mucho menos, pero somos un equipo complicado de batir", aseguró el gijonés.

articles.title: Lionel Messi’s Argentina farewell match is set: Date, opponent, venue, kick-off and everything you need to know
articles.summary: Lionel Messi will play his final match for Argentina on October 6, 2026, against Benin at El Monumental Stadium, marking the end of an illustrious international career with the national team. This article explores the match details, Messi's achievements, and the significance of this farewell event.
articles.body: Lionel Messi's Argentina career is finally approaching its last night. The 39-year-old will pull on the famous blue-and-white shirt one more time in October, with the farewell already carrying a few details that make it unlike an ordinary international friendly, from the opponent and venue to the special No.10 jersey he will wear for the occasion.When and where will Lionel Messi play his final match for Argentina?Messi's final appearance for Argentina is scheduled for October 6, 2026, when the world champions host Benin in Buenos Aires during the current FIFA international window.The match will take place at El Monumental, the home of River Plate and the largest stadium in South America, with the venue capable of holding around 84,000 spectators.It will be the last of Argentina's three FIFA-date friendlies, giving Messi a final opportunity to play in front of his country's supporters before officially closing his international career.Argentina head coach Lionel Scaloni has included Messi in the squad for the match, with the fixture specifically serving as a farewell and tribute to the forward after he announced his international retirement in August.Messi will enter the match with 207 appearances for Argentina, meaning the Benin fixture is expected to become his 208th and final cap for the national team.The opponent will be Benin, a narrow coastal country bordered by Nigeria to the east, Togo to the west, and Burkina Faso and Niger to the north.Benin's senior national team is known as Les Guépards, or The Cheetahs, after officially changing its nickname from The Squirrels. The team traditionally wears a distinctive yellow and green home kit.The side is coached by Gernot Rohr, the German-French manager who took charge in February 2023. Rohr led Benin to the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations, where the team reached the round of 16.The two countries have also crossed paths recently at youth level, with Argentina's U-20 women's team beating Benin 8-0 at the FIFA U-20 Women's World Cup in September 2026.Why is this Lionel Messi's farewell match for Argentina?Messi's final appearance brings the curtain down on an international career that has lasted more than two decades and produced records, major trophies and the defining achievement of his career with Argentina: the 2022 World Cup in Qatar.The forward currently holds Argentina's national-team records with 125 goals and 68 assists, and his 207 appearances before the Benin match already place him at the top of the country's appearance list.His international trophy collection also includes Olympic gold in 2008, consecutive Copa América titles in 2021 and 2024, and the Finalissima in 2022, before Argentina won the World Cup later that year."One last match. A jersey for a lifetime."Messi has now confirmed that his final Argentina appearance will come with a special shirt. In a message shared ahead of the farewell, he wrote: "One last match. A jersey for a lifetime."A newly released video shows Messi replacing a standard Argentina shirt with a special Adidas jersey carrying his name and iconic No.10 in gold, before picking up a pair of white boots.The farewell follows Messi's decision to retire from international football, which he described as painful despite everything he had achieved with the national team."After the time passed since the (World Cup) final, and after thinking carefully about it, I would like to announce to everyone that I will retire from playing with the national team," Messi said when announcing the decision. "It was a painful decision, and it still hurts me deeply, but I understand that the time has come. I swear to you that I have always given my best, not only in the past few years when we won everything, but before that too."Messi also explained what representing Argentina had meant to him throughout his career."I have always fought and left everything on the pitch for this shirt, to bring you happiness and make you feel proud to be Argentines through football."Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Krychowiak: "Recordaré hasta la muerte la final en Varsovia"
articles.standfirst: El exjugador nervionense ha estado en la ciudad deportiva del Sevilla
articles.summary: El exjugador nervionense ha estado en la ciudad deportiva del Sevilla
articles.body: Grzegorz Krychowiak ha vuelto a pisar la ciudad deportiva del Sevilla. El exjugador nervionense ha visitado las instalaciones dentro de un grupo de 22 exjugadores y exjugadoras que están realizando el curso de entrenadores para obtener la licencia UEFA Pro con la PZPN, la Federación de Fútbol de Polonia. También forma parte del grupo Emilia Zdunek, exjugadora del Sevilla FC Femenino que jugó 18 partidos y anotó tres goles en la temporada 2019-2020, recoge el club en su web oficial. El exjugador ha repasado su trayectoria en Nervión en el espacio 'Sólo el Sevilla' de Sevilla FC+. Krychowiak destaca un momento especial por encima de los demás: la final de Varsovia de 2015. "Muchos momentos buenos, fueron dos años aquí y momentos especiales para mí. Es un placer. Fueron dos años impresionantes, con dos copas y una final en Varsovia que es el mejor partido, que recordaré hasta la muerte. En mi país, frente a mi familia, e hice un gol. Encontré muy buena gente: un entrenador especial, jugadores con mucha calidad y buena gente", comentó. También tuvo palabras para Éver Banega: "Fueron dos años trabajando para Banega para que pudiera marcar goles y dar asistencias. Fue el mejor jugador del partido en Varsovia. Es un fenómeno, cuando tienes jugadores como él tienes que entender tu rol en el campo. Yo estaba para correr y él para jugar". Krychowiak regresó al Ramón Sánchez-Pizjuán en marzo de 2024 para grabar un documental sobre su carrera: "Creo que con el tiempo es lo más importante, no cuentan tanto las copas como el respeto de la afición. Te hace sentir especial. Estuve aquí el año pasado para grabar mi película y sentí ese respeto. Gracias a ellos y vamos a ver cómo va la temporada, espero que bien". También se refirió a cómo plantea su futuro como entrenador. "La defensa es lo más importante, pero me gusta jugar al fútbol. Creo que hay que empezar por lo defensivo. Yo era un jugador con carácter y creo que es lo más importante en el fútbol para mí. Puedes perder el balón, cometer un error, pero tienes que trabajar. Puedes tener mucho talento, pero para llegar tienes que trabajar mucho. Tengo una visión del fútbol diferente. He entendido más sobre el jugador que no juega y eso es difícil. En Sevilla jugaba todos los partidos y ganaba. Cuando no juegas, entiendes muchas cosas y aprendes mucho", señaló.

articles.title: What U.S. Presidents Cup players are saying about Trump's Sunday visit to Medinah
articles.summary: Donald Trump plans to attend the 2026 Presidents Cup at Medinah on Sunday. Fans should plan for extra security and delays.
articles.body:
President Donald Trump has a sports weekend that would make many fans jealous.

On Saturday, he's set to be in Knoxville, Tennessee, for the Texas at Tennessee football game. Then on Sunday, Trump will head to Medinah No. 3, site of the 2026 Presidents Cup , to take in Sunday singles action outside of Chicago.

What does that mean for the players and fans attending on Sunday? Expect extra security measures, especially in and around wherever the President will be. At last year's Ryder Cup, fans had to take extra security measures when Trump watched play begin Friday in the afternoon session. There were multiple extra screenings before going into the first tee grandstands, so for those planning to be in attendance, plan extra time to move around the venue during singles.

Many players were asked in the lead-up to the start about the President's visit to Medinah. Here's what they had to say.

Presidents Cup 2026: Best photos from Thursday at Medinah Country Club

"I think it would be great to have the President out and hopefully gets the crowd going. I'm expecting the crowd to be loud and behind us this week and that's what makes playing home team events so fun."

"Like I said, being an American and having the President of the United States coming to watch you play golf is something that as a kid you don't ever imagine or fathom happening. I just think it's pretty amazing. He's our commander in chief, and it's going to be definitely really exciting on Sunday."

"He made a guest appearance at Bethpage as well. I'm sure Secret Service wasn't pumped that he made an early announcement on where he's going to be, (laughter). But they'll do a nice job to keep him safe.

"But, yeah, it's awesome that our president loves golf and supports USA."

"Obviously he's a huge supporter of golf, and at the end of the day it's cool to see the President show up for an event like this."

"I think for me personally, anyone who's the president of this country, I respect that position, obviously. I've actually got to spend some time with President Trump and we've played golf together a few times. I think you just have a ton of respect for that position, and being an American, I think it's very important that we do support our president, regardless of your political views. I think if you look at our country now, it seems more divided than ever, and hopefully we can get back to the point where all Americans come together and we're all trying to kind of reach the same goal."

"I think everyone, you know, whoever the president is, if they care enough to come watch us play golf, that's pretty cool. So I know we're excited, and we're going to go try to put on a good performance for everyone."

Cameron Jourdan is an assistant editor of Golfweek, covering college and amateur golf, the PGA Tour and plenty more. Follow Cameron on X/Twitter (@Cam_Jourdan) or Instagram (@GolfweekJourdan).

articles.title: England captain Harry Kane says he could become an NFL kicker while playing in MLS, drops Golf dream
articles.summary: England captain Harry Kane reveals his shift from aspiring professional golfer to NFL kicker after experiencing the gap in skill levels, while still focusing on his stellar football career with Bayern Munich and England.
articles.body: Harry Kane has already spent much of his career planning for what comes after football, but the England captain has now admitted that one of his long-held ambitions has changed while another remains firmly on the table. Kane has given up on the idea of becoming a professional golfer, yet he still believes an NFL kicking career could be realistic, potentially even allowing him to combine the two sports if he eventually plays in MLS.Kane has finally given up on his dream of becoming a professional golferKane has long been one of football's most prominent golf enthusiasts, regularly playing at some of the leading courses and reportedly holding a 1.9 handicap. He has previously spoken about the possibility of pursuing golf professionally once his football career ends, but the England captain now admits that watching the professionals and actually playing alongside them has changed his perspective.The subject came up after Kane posted an Instagram video showing himself chipping golf balls from a luxury yacht in the Caribbean during his post-World Cup holiday.He had previously maintained a "never say never" attitude towards taking up golf full-time, but his latest assessment was considerably less optimistic."I toy with that in my head. I watch golf and think, 'I could be there'. Then I go out and play, and I am like, 'No, there's no way'," Kane told The Sun."I play off two. I am a member at Wentworth and I shoot ten over."Kane's handicap and regular rounds have given him a serious interest in the sport, but he knows the gap between being a very good amateur and competing professionally is substantial."Then I watch the pros, who played there last week, and 20 under wins it. I think I'll stick to football, to be honest."Kane has also previously played golf with Donald Trump in Palm Beach, illustrating how seriously he takes the sport away from football, but his latest comments suggest that a professional career in golf is no longer something he expects to pursue.For now, football remains his priority, with Kane still performing at the highest level for both Bayern Munich and England.The NFL is the post-football career Kane still believes could workWhile Kane has effectively closed the door on professional golf, he remains interested in another sport that has fascinated him for years: American football.The Bayern Munich striker is a major NFL fan and supporter of the New England Patriots, and his interest has become personal enough that he named his dogs after NFL stars Tom Brady and Russell Wilson.Kane has previously discussed becoming an NFL kicker after retiring from football, and he believes the transition could be more realistic than moving into professional golf because of the similarities between his current role and the demands of kicking in American football."I take penalties and it is a very similar pressure and technique. I would be closer to that more than any other sport," Kane said.He also has the backing of someone who understands the position. Former Kansas City Chiefs punter and Super Bowl champion Dustin Colquitt said in 2025 that Kane "would do fantastic" as a kicker and offered to train him.Kane now says he would approach the challenge seriously rather than treating it as a novelty."That is something I will try and look at a bit more seriously. It all depends on what happens in my career over the next five or six years.""The NFL is a lot more realistic than the golf one, let's put it that way."He believes he would need significant preparation before attempting to enter the sport professionally, despite the apparent similarities between football striking technique and NFL kicking."If I were to do it, it is something I would take seriously. I would take six months to a year to try and practice before."Kane has even identified a potential route that could make the idea easier to explore, with a future spell in MLS potentially allowing him to remain involved in football while training for an NFL opportunity."Maybe if I am in the MLS in the future, or somewhere like that, it might be a thing where you could connect the two."Kane is still focused on extending his football careerFor all the discussion about what Kane might do after football, retirement is not particularly close to his thoughts at present.The 33-year-old is once again in outstanding form, having already scored six goals for Bayern Munich this season, following a previous campaign in which he scored 73 goals for club and country.That extraordinary scoring record has placed him among the leading candidates for the Ballon d'Or, with the award ceremony scheduled for October 26 in London. Kane has admitted that he would love to win the prize, although he believes the timing is not ideal.He is also approaching another major milestone with England. Kane has 121 caps and will face world champions Spain at Wembley in the first of four Nations League matches over an 11-day period.If he features in all four fixtures, he will reach 125 England appearances, drawing level with record holder Peter Shilton. Kane could then break Shilton's record as early as England's November fixtures against Croatia or Spain.Away from international football, Kane has also revealed that he is close to signing a new contract with Bayern Munich, further emphasising that his immediate future remains firmly centred on playing rather than retirement planning.He knows that his career will eventually end, but Kane does not want to spend the remaining years looking too far ahead."But again, it is in the back of my mind because, right now, I am feeling that I want to play for as long as I can here," he said."I think sometimes it is easy to get to my age, 33, to start thinking about retirement or the future.""But I am trying to extract everything I can from the last two, five or ten years."For now, that means more goals for Bayern and England, while the NFL remains a possibility for later and professional golf has been left behind.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Former college football player dies at 23
articles.summary: He played college football at Ohio in 2025.
articles.body:
Former college football player Jaymar Mundy has died, La Salle high school football announced on X. He was 23.

Mundy earned All-State honors at La Salle before going on to play at multiple FBS schools.

"To our Champion. To our Teammate. To our Friend. To our Brother. Our hearts are broken as we mourn the loss of Jaymar Mundy," La Salle football said. "Our thoughts and prayers are with his family, friends, teammates and all who loved him. Forever a Lancer. Forever our Brother. Rest in Peace, Jaymar."

Mundy started his college football career at Miami ( Ohio ) in 2021, appearing in three games and recording two tackles. He then transferred to Hutchinson Community College for two seasons.

Mundy appeared in 19 games across two seasons at Hutchinson, recording 21 tackles, 2.5 tackles for loss, an interception and a pass breakup.

A three-star JuCo prospect, Mundy signed with Western Kentucky for the 2024 season. He played in four games and finished with five tackles for the Hilltoppers.

In 2025, Mundy played for the Ohio Bobcats , appearing in five games and recording four tackles.

Ohio head coach John Hauser remembered Mundy in a post on X.

"Heartbroken," Hauser said. "Jaymar was a great person. He made everyone's day better. He cared so much about the success of his teammates. I will miss him greatly."

articles.title: Roberto Carlos pays tribute to ‘mentor’ Mazzola and claims ‘Inter are extremely strong’
articles.summary: Roberto Carlos has remembered Sandro Mazzola as the man who shaped his brief but formative spell in Italian football, describing the Inter great as his secon...
articles.body:
Roberto Carlos has remembered Sandro Mazzola as the man who shaped his brief but formative spell in Italian football, describing the Inter great as his second teacher.

Speaking at the Portugal Football Summit, with quotes via CalcioMercato , the former Inter and Real Madrid left-back reflected on the relationship days after Mazzola's death at the age of 83 .

"I learned a lot from Sandro Mazzola. He was practically my second teacher in Italy . Always very kind," he said. "He had a worldwide reputation, he is one of those people you learn a lot from, and in the end you win a match and you dedicate it to him. He always told me: 'Play with joy, play happy.' That was the most important thing for us."

Sandro Mazzola wearning an Inter shirt (Inter.it)

Roberto Carlos: 'Italy can go back to being what they were'

Roberto Carlos also gave his verdict on the state of the Italian game, with the national team beginning a rebuild under Roberto Mancini after a third consecutive World Cup absence.

"Italian football? I think the time has come for change. Italy have always been at World Cups and have always had great players. I think they can now go back to being the Italy of old."

He was similarly complimentary about his former club, though he stopped short of backing them for the biggest prize.

"Inter are now an extremely strong team. They have always been a strong team, but I think in the last five years Inter have always been at a very high level. Against Real we saw an Inter side with the mentality to always win. I liked them a lot. Can they win the Champions League? Well, I work for Real Madrid and I think we should win it."

Roberto Carlos spent a single season at Inter in 1995-96 before Massimo Moratti sold him to Real Madrid, a decision widely regarded as one of the worst in the club's history. He went on to win four La Liga titles and three Champions Leagues in Spain , and remains attached to Real in an ambassadorial capacity.

articles.title: Texas A&M coach Mike Elko's advice to his struggling quarterback Marcel Reed: 'Relax and play'
articles.summary: Reed's accuracy has wavered, and injuries have thinned the Aggies' playmakers. Elko says the quarterback can relax and play to his ability.
articles.body:
COLLEGE STATION - Marcel Reed took over as Texas A&M 's quarterback full time two years ago when he replaced Conner Weigman and led the Aggies to a 38-23 victory over LSU .

Since that game on Oct. 26, 2024, Reed has led Texas A&M to the program's first College Football Playoff appearance and produced only the second 11-win season this century.

But Reed's start to 2026 hasn't been ideal as he has struggled with consistency going into this week's game at LSU .

Coach Mike Elko said there's a "plethora of things" that could explain Reed's inconsistent start. But there's one thing he feels is at the top of the list.

"I think probably more than anything, it's a kid who's pressing," Elko said after Saturday's loss to Kentucky . "There's a lot of noise. He feels like he's got to defend himself a lot. That's not an excuse, but that's the reality."

Elko said the "pressing" is visible, and can be seen in his throws. Reed's accuracy against Kentucky was scattershot, missing multiple easy throws, including a layup fourth-down toss that would have moved the chains for the Aggies.

Instead, Kentucky got the ball back and soon scored to go up 28-7. Texas A&M would lose 31-21.

After Saturday's loss to the Wildcats, Reed talked about both the physical and the mental side of his game. He noted his problems feel more mental than physical at this point, and that is something he can change going forward.

"The way for me to get out of that is just calm myself down and obviously tell myself I can make those throws because I know I can make those throws and just do it," Reed said.

Elko also said there's also things he and the coaching staff can do to help unlock Reed and get him to stop pressing. He noted that Reed has played well in two-minute drill situations.

"I've got to get him mentally to a place where he can really cut it loose and feel free and play," Elko said. "I think that more than anything right now is the issue with him. It's like a pitcher sometimes who struggles to throw strikes. It's just growing on him, and he's got to be able to relax and play the way he's capable of."

Through the first three games of the season, Reed is 62 of 104 (59.6%) with 632 passing yards, six touchdowns and three interceptions plus another 117 yards on the ground.

But it hasn't been all bad to start the season. Reed has played really well for stretches during the first quarter of the season.

Wide receiver Mario Craver also said Reed is a better player than he was last year.

"He's got a lot better," Craver said. "I'm not gonna back on that. He's definitely got a lot better in every aspect of the game."

The offense also has been without some of its key playmakers. Wide receiver Ashton Bethel-Roman and running back Jamarion Morrow both missed the Kentucky game. Wide receiver and returner Terry Bussey suffered a season-ending injury on the first play of the game versus the Wildcats and then running back KJ Edwards got hurt as well.

That's two of the team's top three running backs and two of their top four wide receivers gone from Reed's disposal.

LSU presents as good of an opportunity for Reed to reset as any going forward. The first road game of the year against a team he's beaten twice in the past two years, albeit one with a new coaching staff and roster.

It won't be easy by any means but Elko believes in Reed.

"I have a lot of confidence in Marcel," Elko said. "I believe in Marcel. Marcel is our quarterback."
